raw_response:
I am old now, and with only 3 mu and just myself at home, I do not dare make big changes. Cotton is what I know, and on such a small piece of land I can still manage it by hand if needed. I have seen many years: if I save too much on fertilizer, the plants stay weak and the bolls are fewer; if I spend too much, it is hard to get the money back when cotton price is not good. So this year I will still plant cotton on all 3 mu, around the usual time in mid to late April, using the variety I can buy locally and that people nearby also plant. I will prepare the land simply, put some fertilizer at the start, then add a bit later when the plants are growing strongly. Since I have well water, I will keep irrigation for the important times, but I will not water too many times because pumping costs money. For pests, cotton cannot be left alone, so if I see aphids or bollworm pressure, I will spray, and I will also use herbicide once to reduce hand weeding because my labor is limited.
